newsitem.title: USA: Fremont extends, again, tender for Kerr.
newsitem.headline: Fremont extends, again, tender for Kerr.

text.p: Fremont Acquisition Co said Tuesday that it has decided to extend its all cash tender offer for both preferred and common shares of Kerr Group, after Kerr reached an agreement with the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp (PBGC).
Fremont said in a statement that the offer now expires at midnight EDT on Monday, August 25.

The PBGC runs the pension fund for Kerr, and according to Fremont, has agreed to withdraw its lawsuit now pending in U.S. district court in the eastern district of Pennsylvania to terminate Kerr's retirement plan.

Under the terms of the agreement, Kerr agreed to: 1) future enhanced pension plan contributions; 2) grant to the PBGC a second lien on substantially all of the assets of Kerr; 3) various restrictions on future secured indebtedness; and 4) provisions regarding notice of certain events.

Freemont said that it expects the definitive agreement between Kerr, a plastic packaging producer, and the PBGC, which is currently being negotiated to be executed before the expiration of its tender offer.

As of midnight EDT August 18, Fremont said 90 percent of Kerr's oustanding common stock, 61 percent of oustanding preferred stock and 78 percent of common stock oustanding on an as-converted, fully-diluted basis have been tendered.
